content.text: The DnD 5.5 Lupin gives us a taste of werewolf flavor in a player-friendly package, encouraging players to dive into combat and howl at their problems. The Lupin’s signature Howl feature is a powerful area debuff which can turn the tides of encounters with a single Bonus Action, allowing players to quickly overcome groups of enemies.

However, despite how good howl is, the Lupin does come with some big limitations. Feral Pounce is largely useless for the vast majority of characters, especially in a world where Weapon Mastery exists and can reposition or trip enemies just as well, if not better. Werewolf Instincts provides an extra skill, but a limited skill list always means that many characters may not have a good option to choose. Howl, as wonderful as it is, has a range of just 15 feet and the DC is Constitution-based, so many characters might see their save DC fall behind as they gain levels, and many classes will need to get dangerously close to melee to use Howl.

			“Punch and Grab” feature. As a DM, I would force the player to use one

			additional discrete option rather than saying “when you choose X, you also

			full grapple/shove combo in two Unarmed Strikes without giving up damage,
			which is pretty great.

content.text: Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but Howl is still good and an extra skill never hurts. Howl might be especially useful for the Artillerist, allowing you to debuff enemy saves before hitting them with the flamethrower option of your canons and/or Fireball. Melee builds will likely save Howl to help set up combos with other party members.

A typical Strength/Constitution Barbarian build is perfect for the Lupin. Feral Pounce lets you knock enemies prone without giving up all of your damage output, but you can also use a Shove or Topple weapon, so there’s little unique value there. Werewolf Instincts gives you an extra skill so that you’re more useful outside of combat. Howl is perfect for setting up combos, but the competition for your Bonus Action means that you likely can’t use it the first round of combat unless you’re okay waiting to Rage. Imposing Disadvantage on enemies’ attack rolls also offsets the drawback of Reckless Attack, which is nice.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but Howl is still good and an extra
	skill never hurts. Howl might be especially useful for melee builds,
	especially if you can follow it with save-or-suck spells like Hypnotic
	Pattern.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but Howl is still good and an extra
	skill never hurts. Howl might be especially useful for melee builds,
	especially if you can follow it with save-or-suck spells like
	Blindness/Deafness.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but Howl is still good and an extra
	skill never hurts. Howl might be especially useful for melee builds,
	especially if you can follow it with save-or-suck spells. Even at low levels,
	options like Entangle can have a huge impact.

Remember that Feral Pounce only works with Unarmed Strikes. The attacks in
	the stat blocks of beast are not Unarmed Strikes, so you can’t use Feral
	Pounce with them.

Feral Pounce is usable for Strength-based melee builds, but you can use a Shove or Topple weapon, and the Fighter’s features make that an easier option than it is for literally anyone else. Howl is perfect for setting up combos, and can debuff enemy attacks if you find yourself getting swarmed. The extra skill will give you some more options outside of combat, which is always nice.

Feral Pounce allows you to knock enemies Prone without giving up your damage
	output, which is great. If you add the Grappler feat, you can knock enemies
	Prone and then Grapple them, both without giving up your normal attack damage.
	The extra skill is always welcome, especially since Perception and Stealth are
	both great choices for the Monk.

Howl competes for space with the Monk’s other Bonus Action features, so just
	remember to use it more like a scalpel and less like a sledgehammer. If you’re
	getting swarmed and somehow can’t get away, Patient Defense is often a better
	defensive choice because it doesn’t allow a save, but Howl also benefits your
	allies. If you’re fighting a tough opponent, Howl can impose Disadvantage on
	their saves, making it much easier to hit them with Stunning Fist.

Feral Pounce is usable for any Strength-based build, but you can also use a
	Topple or Shove weapon, so there’s little added value there. The extra skill
	is nice, but none of the skill options are great for the Paladin (Stealth is
	good for Dexterity-based builds).4 Howl is the only real value here, but Howl
	is also really good.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but the extra skill is great, and Howl
	is excellent. Howl is great if you’re getting swarmed or if you’re about to
	cast an offensive spell like Conjure Barrage or Steel Wind Strike.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but the extra skill is great. Howl won’t provide a ton of value for you and competes for space with Cunning Action, but it’s great for setting up combos with your allies.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but Howl is still good and an extra
	skill never hurts. The only issue with Howl is that the range is short, so you
	essentially need to dive into melee to use it, and Sorcerers don’t belong in
	melee.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but Howl is still good and an extra
	skill never hurts. Howl is especially useful for Pact of the Blade builds
	planning to fight in melee. The only issue is competition for your Bonus
	Action, which is an issue for many Warlock builds which rely on spells like
	Hex or other subclass features that use your Bonus Action.

Feral Pounce will be useless for you, but Howl is still good and an extra
	skill never hurts. The only issue with Howl is that the range is short, so you
	essentially need to dive into melee to use it, and Wizards don’t belong in
	melee.

The Bladesinger is a notable exception. You’re decently durable with
	Bladesong running, making it easy to jump into melee and use Howl. Resist the
	urge to swing a weapon once you’ve howled. Instead, use a save-or-suck spell.
	Winning a fight in one turn is much more impactful than stabbing things, even
	if you’re singing and dancing.
